# One-Year New Testament Chronological Bible Study

Welcome to a year-long journey through the entire New Testament in chronological order. Over 52 weeks, you will read all 260 chapters of the New Testament — not in the order they appear in your Bible, but in the order the events actually happened and the letters were actually written.

"All Scripture is God-breathed and is useful for teaching, rebuking, correcting and training in righteousness." — 2 Timothy 3:16

# Getting Started

  • How to Use This Study
  • Why Chronological Order?

# Phase 1: The Coming of Christ (Weeks 1-4)

The story begins before Bethlehem — with eternity. John's cosmic prologue, the angelic announcements, and Jesus' birth, childhood, baptism, temptation, and the opening days of his ministry.

Week Title Overview
1 The Word Became Flesh Week 1
2 A Child Is Born Week 2
3 Tested and Called Week 3
4 Ministry Begins Week 4

# Phase 2: The Galilean Ministry (Weeks 5-11)

Jesus bursts onto the scene in Galilee — teaching with authority, healing the sick, casting out demons, and calling disciples. The Sermon on the Mount, the great parables, and the feeding of the five thousand all unfold here.

Week Title Overview
5 Authority Revealed Week 5
6 Words of Power Week 6
7 Parables of the Kingdom Week 7
8 Miracles and Mission Week 8
9 Bread of Life Week 9
10 Who Do You Say I Am? Week 10
11 Life in the Kingdom Week 11

# Phase 3: The Road to Jerusalem (Weeks 12-16)

Jesus turns his face toward Jerusalem. Conflict with the religious leaders intensifies. He teaches in parables of grace, confronts hypocrisy, and prepares his disciples for what lies ahead.

Week Title Overview
12 Conflict and Compassion Week 12
13 Parables of Grace Week 13
14 Signs and Confrontations Week 14
15 The Final Week Begins Week 15
16 Olivet Discourse Week 16

# Phase 4: Passion and Resurrection (Weeks 17-20)

The climax of human history. The Last Supper, Gethsemane, the trials, the cross, the empty tomb. Four weeks immersed in the most important events ever recorded.

Week Title Overview
17 The Upper Room Week 17
18 Gethsemane and Trial Week 18
19 The Cross Week 19
20 He Is Risen Week 20

# Phase 5: The Early Church (Weeks 21-41)

The risen Christ ascends. The Spirit falls at Pentecost. The church explodes across the Roman world. Paul's missionary journeys and letters are woven into the Acts narrative at their historical writing points.

# Phase 6: Letters to the Churches & Revelation (Weeks 42-52)

The final phase covers Paul's pastoral letters, the great theological treatise of Hebrews, the general epistles, and the apocalyptic vision of Revelation — the story's glorious conclusion.

# Quick Stats

  • Total weeks: 52
  • Total reading days: 260
  • NT chapters covered: All 260
  • Daily commitment: ~25-30 minutes (reading + commentary + reflection)
  • Grace days: 2 per week for catch-up or deeper study
